summary: Completed the initial evidence-backed review of YASKAWA Electric's Frankfurt ordinary shares after the 2026-07-29 RSI-oversold transition. YEC.F fell 36.22% from July 1 to EUR 25 and RSI reached 28.53, but the close remained above the lower Bollinger band, volume was not abnormal, and only 30 shares traded. Yaskawa's Q1 revenue rose 10.6% and strong semiconductor orders preserve the operating thesis, while operating profit fell 19.2% and Robotics profit fell 82.3% amid ERP disruption and European restructuring. A bounded 16x-20x forward-EPS scenario remains below the monitored mark, and the Frankfurt line's sparse turnover is a hard liquidity blocker. The assessment is medium-confidence ineligible. No strategy or idea refresh was created because the full strategy gate failed and neither the payload nor an accepted canonical relationship names an idea.

evidence.source: PaperTrader deterministic market and indicator caches
evidence.claim: YEC.F closed at EUR 25 on 2026-07-29, down 36.22% from EUR 39.20 on 2026-07-01. RSI was 28.53, the close remained above the EUR 21.83 lower Bollinger band, volume anomaly was 0.71, and rsi_oversold was the sole transition. Only 30 shares traded on July 29; eight of 21 July sessions and 125 of 254 cached sessions had zero volume. The canonical source-price hash is 13913fe9f36b6c39970bc802b6f80acc2755effa73cd8b31d7606adf7e8f16a8.

Yaskawa reported Q1 revenue of JPY 138.982 billion, up 10.6%, operating profit of JPY 8.486 billion, down 19.2%, and profit attributable to owners of JPY 5.445 billion, down 21.7%. It retained FY2026 guidance of JPY 580 billion revenue, JPY 60 billion operating profit, JPY 47 billion owner profit, and JPY 181.21 EPS. Cash was JPY 57.6 billion, current and non-current bonds and borrowings were JPY 104.7 billion, and the equity ratio was 58.8%.

The issuer briefing showed Motion Control revenue up 21.5% and operating profit up 50.1%, while Robotics revenue rose 2.0% and operating profit fell 82.3%. Yaskawa attributed group profit pressure to ERP-related production disruption, higher indirect expenses, and European restructuring, providing a plausible operating-risk contributor to the alert-period decline without establishing thesis invalidation.

Management reported semiconductor-related AC-servo orders up more than 200% year on year and semiconductor Robotics orders up 141%, with no ERP-related suspension of order intake or observed customer switching. It expected operations to return largely to normal in July and stabilize in August, making delivery conversion and Robotics-margin recovery the next decisive tests.
